source.interpretation: MAPPPD documentation defines nests as breeding pairs.

source_audit.roy1: Cape Royds is site ROYD and has nest counts.
source_audit.crozier_parent: CROZ: Cape Crozier exists but has no nest-count records in the pinned snapshot.
source_audit.accuracy_documentation: MAPPPD documents accuracy as a traditional 5-point census precision score but the package documentation used here does not establish an ordering rule suitable for selecting among duplicate same-site/year counts.

frozen_resolution.same_component_year_duplicate: If a component site has more than one finite nest count in the same year, mark that component-year unavailable; do not average, select by count value, or choose by accuracy score.
frozen_resolution.cape_royds: Use ROYD count only when exactly one finite nest count exists that year.
frozen_resolution.cape_bird: Sum BRDN + BRDM + BRDS only when each of the three components has exactly one finite nest count that year.
frozen_resolution.cape_crozier: Sum CRZE + CRZW only when each of the two components has exactly one finite nest count that year. Do not use empty parent site CROZ.
frozen_resolution.complete_control_year: For the primary individual-choice analysis, colony-size control is available only when all three reconstructed colony totals are available in the predictor year.
frozen_resolution.transform: Use log1p reconstructed breeding-pair count. Within each predictor year, z-standardize across Royds, Bird, and Crozier for the conditional choice model.

primary_alignment.reason: Use only pre-settlement colony size and align it to the same year as the frozen performance predictor.

claim_boundaries: Component summation is a source-semantic reconstruction, not a new ecological result.
Do not fill incomplete component years with parent-site values, temporal interpolation, or ratios from adjacent years.
Do not select among duplicate counts using the magnitude that improves the movement model.
If this fail-closed rule leaves insufficient first-breeding events under the existing minimum-information gate, stop rather than relaxing the rule.
